Gut-check moves: Dolphin above Whale (#1 in both favorite polls and YouGov; Whale leads only on word frequency); Sea Turtle 15 to 5 (#1-2 in both visitor/reader polls; compound name depresses fame signals); Orca 13 to 8 (most pageviews of any sea animal, named apart from 'whale'); Stingray 22 to 10 (Tellwut #3, gut); Starfish 29 to 11 (no poll offered it; fame split across 'starfish'/'sea star'); Clownfish ~24 to 17 ('Nemo' recall; Tellwut 'ornamental fish' 8%). Demotions: Penguin 4 to 18 (a bird many won't count; rank came from Wikipedia and YouGov UK); Coral off (rarely named as a creature; Ngram from 'coral reef' and the colour); Tuna and Oyster off (food-word inflation). Beluga is an alias of Whale; 'otter' sits on Sea Otter.
confidence: Medium-low on exact order, medium on who is in the 24. Shark, Dolphin, Whale solid; Octopus, Sea Turtle, Jellyfish, Seal, Orca well supported for the top 8. No US national multi-species poll exists: Harris 2004 gave only its top two, Tellwut and Big Island Now are fixed-option, partly self-selected (Big Island is Hawaii-local), and the fame signals are noisy. Positions 9-24 lean on gut check plus fame data. Near misses: Beluga (alias on Whale), Sea Urchin, Coral, Tuna, Anglerfish, Pufferfish, Swordfish, Barracuda, Sea Anemone.
